{{advert|date=May 2013}} {{short description|UK company}}{{Company | name = InspecVision | logo = InspecvisionLogo.png | type = Private limited Company | industry = Manufacture of optical precision instruments | hq_location_city = Newtownabbey | hq_location_country = Northern Ireland, UK | website = https://inspecvision.com/ | footnotes = https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/NI045832 https://inspecvision.com/contact/ }} '''InspecVision Ltd.''', established in 2003, is a UK [[engineering]] company based in [[Mallusk]], [[Northern Ireland]]. It is a manufacturing company that produces [[computer vision]] [[inspection]] systems. The company is one of several local companies created as spinoffs or inspired by research conducted at the [[Queen's University of Belfast]].Armstrong P.J. and Antonis J.(2000). ECCV 2000, Book Series Lecture Notes in Computer Science, {{ISBN|978-3-540-67686-7}} == Technology == InspecVision specializes in the design and manufacture of [[Plane (mathematics)|2D]] and [[Three-dimensional space|3D]] [[computer vision]] based measurement systems for [[inspection]] and [[reverse engineering]]. The product range includes the Planar 2D, the SurfScan, the Opti-Scan [[3D scanning|3D]], and the Acuity.{{Citation needed|date=December 2023}} While there are many manufacturers of 3D [[computer vision]] systems, these systems utilize either [[3D scanner|3D scanning]] technologies or a moving camera to measure an object or scene.Pham D.T. and Alcock R.J. (2003). Smart Inspection Systems: Techniques and Applications of Intelligent Vision. Academic Press. {{ISBN|0-12-554157-0}}. InspecVision Ltd. produces primarily 2D or 2&1/2D as well as 3D [[computer vision]] systems. Customers include manufacturers of 2D and 3D components such as [[sheet metal]] components, [[O-ring|O-rings]], [[gaskets]] or plastic moldings. InspecVision has developed a technology which requires no moving parts, rather a single fixed ultra-high resolution [[digital camera]] is used to measure the entire object with a single image.[http://www.ferret.com.au/articles/E7/0C042CE7.asp Ferret, Australia]
 These systems perform measurement times that are usually much less than a second. A completely static system also precludes the rigorous re[[calibration]] requirements of other moving camera or [[computer vision]] systems.{{Cite web|url=http://www.thefabricator.com/article/shopmanagement/moving-beyond-the-traditional-coordinate-measuring-machine|title=Moving beyond the traditional coordinate measuring machine|last=Dr. Jan|first=Antonis|date=May 2016|website=thefabricator.com|publisher=FMA Communications, Inc.|access-date=November 29, 2016}} The InspecVision 2D inspection system, Planar, is the world's fastest. Using only a table, lights, and a PC, it can take hundreds of thousands of measurements in just 0.2 seconds.{{Cite web |title=Machinery Features Articledetailaspxarticleid=150292 {{!}} Machinery |url=http://www.machinery.co.uk/machinery-features/automated-2d-part-measurement-systems-from-keyence-ogp-zeiss-and-inspecvision/150292/ |url-status=dead |access-date=February 13, 2017 |website=www.machinery.co.uk |archive-date=February 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170214002944/http://www.machinery.co.uk/machinery-features/automated-2d-part-measurement-systems-from-keyence-ogp-zeiss-and-inspecvision/150292/ }} There are no moving components and the measurements are taken using a very high resolution camera, which scans parts placed on a backlit glass surface. It can be used for inspection and reverse engineering of flat opaque and semi-transparent parts. The Planar system has been designed specifically for speed, accuracy and ease of use.{{Cite web|url=http://www.qmtmag.com/display_eds.cfm?edno=3572334|title=InspecVision's Planar checks aircraft specs|date=August 2007|website=Quality Manufacturing Today|publisher=Cranbrook Media Ltd.|access-date=November 29, 2016}} The 2D process can measure every feature completely. Planar can produce multiple report types automatically with minimal input from the operator. To inspect, the operator places the part on the measurement surface and with a single click or scan of a barcode. This [[patent]]ed technology has been the recipient of several international awards, including "Best Quality Control System" at the [http://www.mach06.com MACH 2006] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061013165618/http://www.mach06.com/ |date=2006-10-13 }} MWP Awards{{Cite web |url=http://www.mwpawards.com/Results.aspx |title=Metal Working Production Awards, Results |access-date=2006-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061120114920/http://www.mwpawards.com/Results.aspx |archive-date=2006-11-20 |url-status=dead }} and 2 [http://www.investni.co.uk/smart SMART Awards.][http://www.qub.ac.uk/escience/INI%20RD%20Support%20Final.pdf#search=%22inspecvision%20smart%22 Queen's University of Belfast, Research & Development Technology Transfer Programmes, page 9] The SurfScan integrates with the Planar 2D automatic inspection software to allow inspection of both the parts 2D shape and its 2 ½D features with a single click. The high-resolution digital camera of the measurement system captures more than 20 million data points in one second with a single scan.{{Cite web|url=https://www.qz-online.de/produkte/uebersicht/beitrag/3d-scansystem-surfscan-von-inspecvision-alles-andere-als-flach-1299345.html|title=3D Scansystem Surfscan from Inspecvision|website=QZ-online.de|publisher=Carl Hanser Verlag GmbH & Co. KG.|access-date=November 29, 2016}} The Opti-Scan 3D is a non-contact white light scanning system. The system consists of a projector and a high resolution camera mounted side by side. Scans are achieved by projecting a series of stripes onto the part; the projected stripes are then captured with the camera and the images analyzed to produce a 3D point cloud of the scanned surface. Because the system measures every visible surface every time it scans the part; it is likely to detect minuscule and extra features. In addition, because the optical CMM produces a measurement at every pixel in the camera; it can process the highly ordered data much more easily than the disordered point clouds from laser scanners mounted on traditional CMM devices. The InspecVision Opti-Scan systems use patented technology to create both surface and edge measurements achieving unprecedented levels of accuracy. Opti-Scan 3D can offer you single click inspection, mobile large volume scanning and is also the world's only system that can measure edges in 3D.{{Cite web|url=http://metalworkingnews.info/inspecvision-opti-scan-system-perfect-for-measuring-stamped-or-pressed-parts-and-sheet-metal-that-is-not-completely-flat/|title=InspecVision Opti-Scan system – perfect for measuring stamped or pressed parts and sheet metal that is not completely flat|last=|first=|date=|website=Metal Working News|publisher=BA Crawford Specialised Publications (Pty)
